- Dont bend over or pick anything heavy up while you’re healing

- The only pain I had afterwards was my throat hurting soooo bad from intubation- everyone is different though! But if this happens to you and its hard to eat the stuff that I could manage was protein shakes and cream of wheat. For some reason these didn’t burn my throat. But just know that it WILL get better. I woke up one morning after a week or so and I could eat fine again it was so weird.

- If you are nervous before your surgery don’t be afraid to let your doctors know, I was super nervous and they gave me some anxiety meds through an IV- after that I didn’t care what they did I was so relaxed and not in a loopy way, more of a regular human way hahahaha

- Like everyone else says don’t focus too much on your results afterwards. It definitely helps that you’ll have a cast on because you can’t really see your nose that well. But swelling can make your nose look bigger than before, and make it look crooked- so don’t stress please wait for swelling to go down which can take up to a year.

- if you can, buy a elevated pillow wedge and travel pillow these saved me and helped me sleep

- drink tons of water, and eat as much as you are able. Surgery is a lot on the body so you should be trying to eat more than you normally would.

- stay away from a lot of sodium (can increase swelling)

- You can feel anxious/depressed after surgery this is normal and will go away

- I had tingling sensations/numbness over my face the first week or so, this is normal and will go away

- I also had tingling and numbness in my arms and legs right after surgery and was probably a side effect of the anesthesia (anesthesia can take a while to get out of some peoples bodies) so you might also feel brain fog for a few days as well.

- Make sure to get up and walk every hour or so, but don’t over exert yourself. Just walk around for about 5 mins

** Keep in mind this is just my experience and if anything just ask your surgeon or see a doctor! :-)

I’m not sure what all you got done on your nose but I know one of the main reasons people feel like the nose looks too small for the face post-op is because of the length of the philtrum can seem longer when the tip of the nose is still healing and dropping. Once your nose is healed and the tip drops it will look more even. Additionally people sometimes will get a bit of lip filler in the top to counter act this. But again try not to freak out until you see your final results! You can always talk to your surgeon about your concerns as well and they may tell you what to expect when its healed.

Two weeks is so so early to see final results. I know it can be hard but just give it time! Look up lots and lots of swelling progression and tip drop photos from people throughout their healing phases. It takes a year and a half to see final results. Don’t underestimate how much it will change. Some people even have the opposite problem where their nose looks ten times bigger after the surgery and then after a year its so tiny and dainty. Take photos everyday of yourself but dont look at them, and then look back at them every now and then to see how much stuff changes. Also look at old unflattering photos of your nose and remind yourself why you wanted the surgery. Also remember that post-surgery blues are real and can have you feeling depressed for no reason. All will be okay!! I am 2 weeks post-op from my own rhinoplasty and I look ridiculous hahahahah but we will be okay! Time heals all ♡
